policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the princes' words as a question, "Where is strong drink?", which is the interrogative qere אֵי. The mapped textual_variant note "Another reading is, to desire strong drink" reports the ketiv או (read as a desiderative) as the alternative the ASV did not put in its text, so the note confirms rather than unsettles the choice: the rendered reading is the qere.

ASV "she planteth a vineyard" carries a feminine subject continuing the woman of the verse, matching the qere נָטְעָה (3fs perfect). The ketiv נטע lacks the feminine ending and would be read as a masculine "he planted" or an infinitive, which the ASV wording does not permit. No note bears on this unit.

Qere בַלַּ֣יְלָה and ketiv בליל are the two forms of the same noun for night with the same preposition; both yield "by night". ASV's "Her lamp goeth not out by night" is identical under either, and no note is mapped here, so the base fallback carries the projection.
